[Problem on LeetCode](https://leetcode.com/problems/not-boring-movies/)

## Problem

`Cinema` lists movies with an `id`, a name, a `description` and a `rating`. Report the movies with an odd `id` whose description is not `'boring'`, ordered by rating from highest to lowest.

## Formalisation

Let $C \subseteq \mathbb{N} \times M \times D \times \mathbb{R}$ be the table, with tuples $(i, m, d, r)$. First filter, then project:

$$
\pi_{i,m,d,r}\big(\sigma_{\,i \equiv 1 \ (\mathrm{mod}\ 2)\ \wedge\ d \neq \text{boring}}(C)\big) = \{(i,m,d,r) \in C \mid i \text{ odd},\ d \neq \text{boring}\}.
$$

The projection keeps every column, so here it is the identity and the answer is just the selection.

The ordering is not part of the algebra: a relation is an unordered set, so `ORDER BY` turns the result into a sequence $(t_1, t_2, \dots)$ with $t_k.r \ge t_{k+1}.r$. That is why ordering always comes last, after the set has been built.

## Solution

```sql
SELECT c.id, c.movie, c.description, c.rating
FROM Cinema c
WHERE c.id % 2 != 0 AND c.description != 'boring'
ORDER BY c.rating DESC;
```

## Pitfalls

- **Order by the column the question asks for.** My first version used `ORDER BY c.id DESC`, which passes the example only by coincidence: there, ids 5 and 1 have ratings 9.1 and 8.9, so both orderings agree.
- **`!= 0` is safer than `= 1` for odd numbers.** In MySQL, `-3 % 2 = -1`, so `id % 2 = 1` would miss negative odd ids. Ids here are positive, but the habit is worth keeping. `MOD(id, 2)` behaves the same way.
- **`!=` silently drops NULLs.** If a description were NULL, `description != 'boring'` would be UNKNOWN and `WHERE` would discard the row, even though a missing description is not "boring". To keep such rows, write `(description != 'boring' OR description IS NULL)`.
- **`!=` and `<>` are the same.** `<>` is the SQL standard; both work in MySQL.
